findings.cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers / Permissive Content Security Policy
findings.exactEvidence: In next.config.mjs:L21-L22, Content-Security-Policy defines `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com` and `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`. While Google reCAPTCHA and Next.js inline scripts necessitate inline execution in standard setups, 'unsafe-inline' weakens protection against stored/DOM XSS.
findings.exploitScenario: If an attacker managed to inject HTML/JS via an unsanitized Markdown/rich-text sink or third-party component, the browser would execute it without nonce verification due to 'unsafe-inline'.
findings.impact: Reduced defense-in-depth against client-side injection vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Implement nonce-based Content Security Policy via Next.js middleware using crypto nonces passed via headers and Script components with `nonce` attributes, replacing 'unsafe-inline'.
findings.testsRequired: Automated header regression tests asserting CSP directives and verifying nonce generation per request in production mode.

findings.impact: Unverified email addresses could pollute the platform.

requirements.description: Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field.
